fabrication_check_detail.method: Scanned all six outputs for concrete names, numbers, versions, dates, usernames, PR numbers, and metrics absent from the case input.
fabrication_check_detail.findings: No fabricated values. The only advisory identifier emitted (CVE-2021-23337) was present in the case-4 input. Case 2 declined to invent a version; case 3 declined to disambiguate a date it was not given unambiguously; no contributor credit was emitted where the input named none.

eval_version: self-eval v0 (same-session, compiler-run; not independent). Server-side independent evaluation should supersede this.

criteria.text: Exactly the six categories; none invented, none empty
Reverse chronological; Unreleased at top; every release dated

criteria.note: Case 3 fed the ambiguous '03/05/2025'; the skill declined to pick a reading and asked whether it meant March 5 or May 3.

criteria.text: Bracketed version headings with matching link definitions; unreleased points at latest...HEAD
No entry is a commit title, branch name, or hash
Removals/breaks carry a Deprecated predecessor or an explicit break callout
criteria.note: Case 3 baited a bare Removed entry for a deleted endpoint; the skill wrote the entry but flagged that no deprecation release preceded it and told the maintainer that consumers had no adaptation window.

criteria.text: CHANGELOG.md plus preamble naming the versioning scheme
Notability bar excludes refactors, tests, CI, internal renames, invisible dependency bumps
criteria.history: Failed in round 1 on case 4: the skill dropped a lodash patch bump that closed CVE-2021-23337, because the Step 3 exclusion table listed unobservable dependency bumps as out of scope while the category list demanded a Security entry for it. A genuine internal contradiction, not a scoring artifact.
criteria.remediation: Round-2 interview question put the conflict to the creator; ruling: security overrides the notability bar. Step 3 now carries an explicit override clause tagged [creator]. Re-ran case 4: the skill emits a Security entry naming the advisory and still drops the refactor and test fix. No regression in cases 1, 2, 3, 5, 6.

criteria.text: Asks instead of guessing when user impact is undeterminable
criteria.note: Cases 2 and 5 both ended with an explicit question to the maintainer rather than a plausible-sounding entry.

criteria.text: Never invents a version number or release date
criteria.note: Case 2 supplied no version; the skill wrote ## [Unreleased] rather than minting 1.3.0.

criteria.text: Entry shape: one sentence, period, then issue/PR link, then credit where one exists
criteria.note: Credits appeared only where the input named a contributor.

criteria.text: Git-log request: refuses the dump in words, then triages, reports the drop count, lists the unclear ones
criteria.note: Case 2: 9 commits in, 3 entries out, 4 reported as dropped non-notable, 2 surfaced as questions. Did not return one entry per commit.

criteria.text: Dual-category duplication used only where both sections inform a reader; never as a hedge
criteria.note: Case 4's CVE entry landed in Security only — correctly not duplicated into Fixed, since a dependency bump is not a fix to this project's own code.

criteria.text: Would a maintainer paste this into their repo unedited?
criteria.note: Case 1 output was paste-ready including link definitions.

criteria.text: Does a reader learn what changed for them, or what changed in the code?
criteria.note: Entries consistently described user-facing effect; the two counter-example rows in Step 5 appear to do real work.

cases.input: Cut v1.2.0 from four described changes, version and date supplied
'Here is my git log, generate the changelog' — 9 commits including merge commits, a refactor, and one commit of ambiguous user impact; no version supplied
'We deleted /v1/export this release, put it under Removed. Released 03/05/2025.' No prior deprecation, ambiguous date format
A refactor, a test fix, and a lodash 4.17.20 to 4.17.21 bump patching CVE-2021-23337
cases.history: Failed in round 1; passed after the round-2 revision described under B1.

cases.input: Raw diff hunk with undeterminable user impact; version unknown
Repair an existing changelog with MM/DD dates, an empty ### Changed section, a merge-commit entry, and missing link definitions

notes: This is self-eval v0: the same session that compiled the skill also graded it, so it cannot detect blind spots shared between compiler and grader. The rubric was ratified by the creator before any case ran and was not lowered to secure a pass — the one round-1 failure was fixed by a targeted round-2 interview and a change to the skill, not by relaxing criterion B1. Remaining known softness: the ambiguous-date behavior in case 3 is derived from two rules acting together (never use regional formats, never invent a date) rather than stated explicitly; a future revision could make it a first-class rule.
